A1.justification: Both PDFs contain complete, readable versions of the same APS study. The methods, experiments, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendix D.

before.justification: V1 reports original APS detection results, harmonic-regression analyses, and human-versus-LLM comparisons across English and Chinese corpora, including Tables 1–8.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a repetition audit, structural-length distribution statistics, and a worked WSJ document analysis.

M1.justification: Appendix A, Algorithm 3 changes the written final selection step from returning the regression split t_best to returning a peak found by findPeak(ACF, W, t_best). This is a localized pseudocode correction: peak refinement was already described in v1 Section 3.3, so it does not establish a redesigned implementation or rerun experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use PTB-WSJ, Brown, CTB, RST Discourse Treebank, GCDT, FACE English/Chinese news, and EvoBench XSum. The repetition sample and additional WSJ example remain within this existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The harmonic-regression comparisons retain the same baseline predictors and EDU, sentence, and document scaling variants. Renaming the document column to Whole Text does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 7 adds a diagnostic protocol that randomly samples 150 periodic LLaMA3-70B news documents, approximately 10%, inspects repetition, and reports an adjusted comparison. Existing corpus-level sample sizes, language models, permutation settings, and harmonic-regression configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 extends the existing structural-length analysis from unit averages to full distributions and tail comparisons. Section 7 adds a repetition audit addressing a possible confound, while Appendix D adds a worked analysis of WSJ document #2380. These are targeted supplementary checks within the original study.

E5.justification: Permutation-based confidence thresholds and harmonic-regression coefficient p-value reporting are retained. The new length percentiles are descriptive statistics, and the repetition audit adds no confidence intervals, repeated-run information, or new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their numerical entries. New results include 33.33% of valid periods versus 3.63% of paragraphs exceeding 150 tokens, repetition in 11 of 150 inspected texts, and a reported repetition-adjusted model rate of 27.86% versus 14.80% for humans. Appendix D adds detected periods of 61, 101, and 374 tokens.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 corrects the no-hint/no-valid-period subset from Sigma minus P2 to Sigma minus P1, changing the mathematical set description. The Fourier, autocorrelation, and harmonic-regression equations remain substantively unchanged, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: document-level periodicity detection with APS, periods extending beyond local structural units, and potential usefulness for distinguishing human and generated text. Additional evidence supports these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7 replaces the LLM-coherence/human-memory explanation with repetition and recurring paragraph structures versus flexible human narration. The conclusion adds a topic-scale latent-structure hypothesis. New Ethics Statements identify writing assistance, individual style, and second-language writing as confounds limiting authorship conclusions from periodicity.

D1.justification: V2 adds a Zenodo archive reference alongside the existing GitHub link. Appendix D documents intermediate hints, regression splits, and selected peaks. The direct CTB catalogue footnote is removed, although its dataset citation and identifier remain.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to UID, AutoPeriod, spectral methods, and harmonic regression remain the same. Updated titles, author names, and publication details are bibliographic corrections rather than additions to related work.

P1.justification: V2 copyedits sentences, standardizes period-hint and valid-period terminology, expands affiliations, and changes Sanity-Check to Validity-Check. Ethics Statements, Acknowledgments, and Appendix D are added, while the existing narrative and section order are largely retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is substantially redesigned from period counts with structural-unit averages to four percentage distributions with 90th-percentile markers. New Figures 6–9 provide a substantial visual walkthrough of source text, surprisal, the periodogram, and ACF split-versus-peak refinement. Existing tables are also reformatted or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the long-period evidence through full structural-length distributions, checks repetition as a confound, and clarifies peak selection through the appendix walkthrough. Added archival access information and specific detection cautions improve transparency. These are useful, bounded gains: the central empirical results remain unchanged, and the 150-document repetition audit does not quantify uncertainty in its adjusted comparison.
